reconcile.note: Henry reads Deuteronomy 2:9's protection of Moab as bound to that moment, a stance later reversed once Moab turned to oppress Israel under the judges.

discrepancy.note: Colenso ties Deuteronomy's Moab peace-clause to Moab's late independence, a period predating Jeremiah's oracles condemning Moab to destruction.

quotes.text: Here also we have most probably an indication of the long and flourishing independence of the Moabites in the time of the Deuteronomist.
quotes.attr: John William Colenso (d. 1883), The Pentateuch and Book of Joshua Critically Examined, Vol. III (1863), on Deuteronomy 2:9 and Jeremiah 48:2.

sides.snippet: Yahweh said to me, Don't bother Moab, neither contend with them in battle; for I will not give you of his land for a possession; because I have given Ar to the children of Lot for a possession.
sides.verseText: Yahweh said to me, Don't bother Moab, neither contend with them in battle; for I will not give you of his land for a possession; because I have given Ar to the children of Lot for a possession.

sides.snippet: The praise of Moab is no more; in Heshbon they have devised evil against her: Come, and let us cut her off from being a nation. You also, Madmen, shall be brought to silence: the sword shall pursue you.
